Subject: DPA follow-up — evidence for 'no-model-learning' + subprocessor list

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the call this morning. SignalRise is keen to move to signature but legal has two remaining asks before procurement can sign the DPA redline you sent: 1) operational evidence that our telemetry/interaction data will not be used for model improvement or derivative training; and 2) a certified list (or attestation) of subprocessors involved in inference, KV caching, and telemetry handling (including any cloud infra partners).

Can you provide a short evidence pack we can attach to the DPA? Preferably: an ops runbook summary, proof of KV eviction/transience, and a subprocessor snapshot with roles and ingress/egress boundaries. We're OK with a redacted list for public cloud providers if you include the control descriptions.

Attached: our procurement checklist (procurement_checklist_SR.pdf). Happy to take a short follow-up call if helpful.

Best,
Emma

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (privacy/legal) and David (ops) to assemble the evidence pack. First-pass answers below while we pull the artifacts:  

- Commitment: Redwood will not use SignalRise customer interaction data to improve models unless an explicit, signed training agreement is executed; the DPA redline contains the clause (see §4.c).
- Ops proof: we can provide an operational summary (single-page) describing ephemeral KV cache behavior, eviction timing, and prefix caching controls.
- Subprocessors: we will produce a snapshot with roles (inference, telemetry, storage) and a short description of the contractual controls and regions. Third-party provider endpoints will be redacted to IP ranges where necessary.

We plan to assemble: 1) SignalRise_evidence_summary.pdf (single page); 2) no-learn-evidence_matrix.xlsx (matrix mapping control -> artifact); 3) subprocessor_snapshot.csv (redacted). Expect to share by EOD tomorrow.

If legal at SignalRise needs attestations signed by our security officer, let us know and I will escalate.

Thanks,
Vivek
Director, Customer Success — Healthcare & Regulated Industries
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Emma Lang <emma.lang@signalrise.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up — evidence for 'no-model-learning' + subprocessor list

Emma, Vivek — attaching the evidence matrix and a short explanatory note for SignalRise legal. Key items I want to highlight for SignalRise legal:  

1) No-model-learning: operationally we enforce a service-side flag that marks tenant traffic as non-consumptive. That flag prevents token and gradient capture paths to training pipelines (not just policy); we describe the enforcement layers in the matrix (app layer, runtime router, ETL gate).
2) KV cache: per-tenant ephemeral KV with TTL <= 12 hours for interactive sessions by default; eviction and truncation logs are available for audit on request.
3) Subprocessors: list categorizes subprocessors into (a) inference runtime (managed GPU pools), (b) telemetry/observability (masked/stored metrics only), (c) long-term storage (S3-like, encrypted at rest). Where third-party cloud infra is used, we provide contractual security controls and attestations; we will not disclose exact operational hostnames but will provide region and control mappings.

Attached: SignalRise_evidence_summary.pdf (pdf), no-learn-evidence_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet). If SignalRise needs a signed attestation from our Head of Security, we can provide a short, scoped attestation letter; Marissa will coordinate the signature routing.

Next steps proposed: (A) SignalRise reviews artifacts and indicates any gaps by EOD Friday; (B) If they require attestation, Marissa will pick up and schedule security sign-off; (C) Execute final DPA redline and route DocuSign.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
